527.s: He took up flugelhorn for the Jim Hall quartet and the Oliver Nelson record.
527.q: That happened when I organized the group with Jim Hall. I figured that the trumpet would be too penetrating to play with a guitar ‘cause Jim Hall is not one of those bangers. He never is a loud player. I figured the trumpet would be too dominating, and I had made this record that I had told you…

527.t: Flugelhorn's limits and the invention of the flumpet
527.s: The flugelhorn's dark sound loses power in the high register, so he moved to Monette's flugelhorn-trumpet hybrid.
527.q: Yeah, the flugelhorn has a darker, wider sound than the trumpet. The negative thing is – as long as you stay within the perimeters of it, it’s okay – but basically, I’m a trumpet player and sometimes I feel like I want to play in that range. But the flugelhorn doesn’t work so well if you go into…

527.s: Monette in Portland makes horns for orchestral players; Farmer has played the flumpet since about 1990.
527.q: It’s a guy named David Monette, and he’s located out in Portland, Oregon. He comes here to New York City a lot. He’s a real nut for Mahler symphonies. Mahler uses trumpets a lot. He travels all around just to hear those symphonies. He’s a good friend of Wynton Marsalis also. Basically, he makes…

527.t: Earlier horns and mouthpieces: Besson, Couesnon and Martin
527.s: The flugelhorns, mouthpieces and Martin trumpets he played over the years.
527.q: It was a French Besson, which has a reputation of being one of the best, the French Besson and another French horn called the Couesnon.

96.t: Eldon Benge makes him a cornet
96.s: The Chicago Symphony's Benge hears him at the Brass Rail and makes a cornet for him, puzzled by improvisation.
96.ch: Army cornet and Bix's Bach horn
96.q: a good ear and have the feeling for it naturally. Basic rhythm feeling. And know your harmony and know how to improvise. You have to know all your chords on your instrument as well as being able to hear them, you have to have a good ear.

96.t: A new Benge horn after the war
96.s: After the war Benge replaces his battered horn with a new one; Johnston praises hearing it.
96.ch: Army cornet and Bix's Bach horn
96.q: Yes. Eldon Benge, I came back and my poor Benge horn was all battered up you know from going and travelling all over there over the years, two and a half years in Europe. So I'm playing now the 'Brass Rail' again and Alvin came in one night. He had been in previously and so you know we were talking…

96.t: Difference between a cornet and a trumpet
96.s: He explains the cornet is shorter, mellower and sits closer to the body.
96.ch: Army cornet and Bix's Bach horn
96.q: Very little difference. Both are B Flat instruments in the key of B Flat. And a trumpet is a bit, little longer and the tone is more piercing than a cornet. A cornet is a little shorter and it sort of fits in closer to my body anyway.

245.t: Cornet versus trumpet, shanks and tone
245.s: Government-issue trumpets, cornet shanks, and the differences in tone and blowing between cornet and trumpet.
245.q: Oh yeah, I had a trumpet in, in France. The issues of trumpet in 1918. I had a busher trumpet. Yeah, that was out of press. Really? Yeah. I don't know when they came out, but I know the government issues trumpets. Because, uh, White had a york trumpet. You can see on that picture his trumpet. Got a…

245.s: He still owns the old Conn he played in New Orleans and will keep it.
245.q: Oh, CG con. I still have my old CG con that I used to play back there in New Orleans, you know. Yeah, I still got it. And I'm gonna keep it till I die. Yeah, I think you should.

568.t: Touring to Long Beach and the Conn Wonderhorn
568.s: A band member was left in hospital in California; he met the Wonderhorn maker and says he prefers Conn horns.
568.q: We had to leave Dominic there. We left Dominic there until we got to Long Beach. They kept him in the hospital two weeks. I can't think of that band leader's name, one of the greatest men there was. Then I had the pleasure of shaking hands with the man that made C.G. Conn's first Wonderhorn. That…

568.t: Switching to trumpet and buying Chicago buildings
568.s: He changed horns, bought a Selmer secondhand, and recalls spending his earnings on flat buildings and lots that were later lost.
568.q: I changed, I changed when I got here, didn't I? I was using the Wonder, wasn't I? Yeah. The Wonder was, Herbert L. Clark was his name. Oh, yeah, sure. It's in the Suzy's band. Yeah, he had the band, yeah. He made a horn that the tuning slide was in the back called a Wonder. You could hold it. And…

5.t: When he switched to trumpet; cornet on the records
5.s: He thinks he got a trumpet before Chicago but used his Jay cornet through the Hines years, always open horn.
5.q: About what year, or what band? Let's see, my, I'm trying to think now, when I, did I get, when did I get my first trumpet? I'm, I don't know whether it was before I came to Chicago. I think, I think I, I got a trumpet before I came to Chicago. Pardon, let's see.

5.t: Buying a Harry B. Jay cornet after Muggsy lent his
5.s: The cornet he used for the Morton records was a Chicago-made Jay, bought after Muggsy Spanier left his horn at a 35th Street club.
5.ch: Jelly Roll Morton and other records
5.q: What make did you like? Oh, I think, uh, that was, uh, I believe I made, uh, made, uh, had a trumpet then of, uh, was made here in Chicago. Jay, Harry B. Jay. Oh, yeah. A cornet. I've heard, yeah, let's say Armstrong used one of those. Yes, yeah. It was a cornet. It was a cornet, yeah. I, I, uh,…

574.s: Talk about trombone brands he and others favoured.
574.q: Yeah, nice. But I think C.E. Con got a better trombone than they never. To me, to my days, they used to I know. Like it was a more keener tone than the trombone.

574.t: Buying a Conn trombone and bell size
574.s: He bought a silver Conn in town for sixty-some dollars; discussion of six and seven inch bells.
574.q: I mean would you like the little one? I think, with my experience, about a seven inch ought to be. That ought to be a little bit better. It gives you a heavier tone. About seven. Yeah. That's about the best of all I was playing. I know that's what I would use. Because I knew that I know it's when…

418.t: Old horns versus new: metal, workmanship and salesmanship
418.s: He thinks old instruments sound better because of purer metal, comparing them to a Rolls-Royce versus a Ford.
418.ch: Trombone technique, plunger mute and the California years
418.q: I think that the quality... Well, maybe it's the workmanship, but the metal just don't seem as nice and sturdy as it used to. I guess everybody's trying to save something. You know? But the metal of those old instruments... That's why an old instrument sounds good, because the metal is... They made…

418.t: Old horns versus new: metal, workmanship and salesmanship
418.s: He thinks old instruments sound better because of purer metal, comparing them to a hand-built Rolls Royce against a Ford.
418.ch: Trombone technique, plunger mute and the California years
418.q: I think that the quality -- well into the workmanship, but the metal isn't as -- don't seem as nice and sturdy as it used to. I guess everybody is trying to save something. You know. But the metal of those old instruments -- that's why an old instrument sounds good -- that the metal is -- they've…

240.t: His trumpets and cornets over the years
240.s: He lists the Buescher, Conn and Martin horns he bought, lost or had stolen, and the five he owns now, including a King cornet.
240.q: Oh when I changed over the trumpet, my first trumpet I bought was a busher. I bought that busher in 30. But I didn't like it because it was very keen and very, very long and not knowing better in those days. I didn't know that I wasn't getting, it didn't have, it didn't carry much volume. And…

859.t: Old-time players and George McCullum Sr.'s cornet
859.s: Talk of old George McCullum, his widow keeping his cornet, and Gabriel's own E-flat and B-flat cornets and clarinet in Detroit.
859.q: Well, Suga was over there. Jack Pyee. And Buddy Johnson. And Mr. That other fella. Did you tell anything about George McCullum? Yeah. I don't mean the boy. I'm talking about the daddy.

256.s: The first horn cost $3 at a pawn shop; his current King is some 47 years old and was refurbished once.
256.q: Well, the first horn I had I bought for $3 in the hawk shop. And then I got this thing. This thing is about... I had it overhauled once. I sent it back to King. It's the King H.N. White in Cleveland. I sent it back once and the guy knew me. He says, where'd you get this horn, Bruno? It's from…

35.t: Bunk's Selmer trumpet, cornet and mouthpiece
35.s: Blumberg and Russell discuss how Bunk handled the Selmer, tried Blumberg's King cornet and his mouthpiece.
35.q: I think he liked it. He certainly handled it as if he liked it, but, uh, he tried my cornet. I was playing a King cornet at the caravan one night, and, and, uh, he sounded kind of different on the thing. And, uh, we were all very interested, you know, to hear, uh, how he sounded on it. And, uh, he,…

956.t: His Harry B.J. trombone and the 1926-27 trade with Mike Riley
956.s: Henry shows his silver-plated trombone, tells how he traded instruments in Cleveland at the Elks convention, and mentions having it replated.
956.q: And this fella played banjo and trombone. He had this one, and I had a handmade blessing made in Elkhart, Indiana. I paid $2.25 for the blessing, and he paid $2.25 for that one. And he had a weight, balance weight here.

624.t: Mardi Gras Day with one trumpet; E-flat trumpet and leading
624.s: Brunies led Fisher's band on Mardi Gras, then discusses cornet, the E-flat trumpet, his King horn, and why to carry a straight lead.
624.ch: Playing in clubs and Mardi Gras
624.q: Yes. Yeah, I used to take fishing's band with one trumpet with 10, 12 men. On Mardi Gras Day, early in the morning, 9 o'clock. One time, 8 o'clock. From the Slot House up to the Audubon Park. Oh, and around Canal Street. All in and out different places. People's home. That's the time we used to…

251.t: Floyd's gold orchestra, C.G. Conn horn and Floyd as leader
251.s: Floyd's orchestra had gold instruments; Albert was given a trumpet and rehearsals were frequent; Floyd had faults but was a nice man.
251.q: Right, right. The name of the band was Troy Floyd and his orchestra of gold. Everybody had gold instruments. And I never, I should have kept this, but I don't know why I didn't. C.G. Kahn made me a present of the first long trumpet that was made. And they carried my name on the little pamphlets in…

620.s: When a truck had a piano, the piano led rather than the cornet; he adds a remark about trumpets and cornets.
620.q: He'd come there, he'd be blowing. He'd blow, but the piano was the leader. He'd go there and he'd play. I see now today, everything in the day is cornered leading. The most of the time they didn't have cornered, they had trumpets. They were blowing trumpets at that time. The short ones? Yeah, the…

40.s: He traded trumpet for cornet to fit an old-style group and discusses tone; Kid Howard and Sidney De Paris use both instruments.
40.q: Uh, how do you mean, uh, which, which tone? The trumpet or the clarinet? Oh, I like, I like, uh, I like the Cornet. I like the Cornet. So, you know, you take, uh, these fellows that play, you know, strictly the sweet dance music, uh, they would have to use trumpet. See, it's that, that type of…

839.t: French's old horn and no longer playing
839.s: Talk of how long since French played, his Supertone Bandmaster horn, trying to sell it, and a dental device for playing.
839.q: No, none of them don't. I tried to sell it. They wouldn't buy it. I tried to sell it. I bought it. I bought it on the bar. Say that.

138.t: Old cornets, Alfred's cornet, Johnny Provenzana
138.s: They talk about old silver cornets, Alfred's B-flat cornet, and Johnny Provenzana, who played an E-flat cornet, plus Biloxi musicians.
138.q: Alfred's Cornet. Alfred's Cornet. What kind of Cornet was it? B-Flat. B-Flat. Manuel, his brother-in-law been wanting to buy it, but his wife won't, won't part.

187.t: His first trombone and later horns
187.s: From a horn bought from Williams to a C.G. Conn and a Buescher with larger bore and bell, bought during WPA time.
187.q: First trombone I got it was a busher. No, C.G. Kahn. You want the real first one? I got an old horn out from Donisonville, Professor Claiborne Williams sold me one. You got one from him. But when I came to New Orleans, when I got with Sidney Desby and I used that old horn, I traded it in, I went to…

777.t: E flat versus B flat cornet in the Eureka
777.s: With the Eureka they used B flat solo cornet, not E flat.
777.q: I haven't seen no band with E flat since I left home. Since that bass band at home had that E flat. Mm-hmm. They all used B, voice solo, voice cornet.

288.t: His horns: Holton, Conn and Buescher; cornet to trumpet; banjo, sax, tuba
288.s: Charles describes switching between instruments, getting a Buescher about a year before quitting, and instrumentation changes.
288.q: Yes. The first one was a Holton. Then I bought corn. Then I thought the corn wasn't hard enough, I went back to the Holton. And I used the Holton and it looked like it could stand more punishment, you see. Corn was a little, when you blow a little too hard it looked like it would blast. I didn't…

681.t: Setting up and discussing his father's Conn Victor cornet
681.s: Hirsch shows the interviewer his father's Conn Victor-model horn and its tuning shanks; talk of Tony Fusero and cleaning it.
681.q: The Victor model, it has an automatic change deal in here, playing in A, where you have B-flat and you have A. This is your tuning valve here, where you tune it. It's all stuck now. Okay, let's see. This is for a quick change.

830.t: Cornet versus trumpet and Armstrong wanting little George's gold trumpet
830.s: A cornet is harder to blow than a trumpet; Armstrong wanted to buy little George's gold trumpet, which was stolen; she kept her husband's cornet.
830.q: You know why I started using a trumpet, several, according to the little trumpet, a trumpet is a little easier to blow than a cornet.

573.t: The cornets and trumpets he owned
573.s: He describes his cornets and King trumpets and returning to a cornet.
573.q: I just, any, any, any, any, uh, world I had with CG corn was to go then. Then the next, I had a, a king trumpet I got from Mobile. Then the next, I got a, a king trumpet. I had two king trumpets. And I had some other kind of trumpet. I forgot this kind of trumpet that I had. Well, anyway, I was, I…

858.t: Day job packing instruments and the mellophone
858.s: He has packed instruments for 15 years and earlier for C.G. Conn; a mellophone is explained.
858.q: The Wicked. Musical instrument packer. I've been working at Well Islands now for 15 years. 15 years? Before that I worked for C.G. Conn. For the WPA, pardon, the Ions, I worked for C.G. Conn. I worked for C.G. Conn. I worked for 15 years. Packing instruments, shipping them all over all the other…

639.t: Working at Werlein's and joining the school board
639.s: He tells of the Buescher cornet he tried at Werlein's while playing with Earl Crumb, and of his later years with the school board.
639.q: about to say in the series robot catalog around 1910 I thought I remembered but I'm not quite sure whether it was in that catalog or later I do remember the first time I saw a trumpet in series robot catalog and I remember thinking how ugly it looked it looked like a bugle you know stretched out…

997.s: They examine the silver mellophone his father gave him before he died, discuss how it was held, and his father's records.
997.q: Some of them, yeah they play with the hand in the bell I'm sure they do some of them. Is that the way your father played it? I believe he used to play it. Sometime I've seen him with the hand in the bell.

101.t: The flugelhorn: Miles's fat girl and rebuilding it for Selmer
101.s: Miles, Berry and Rogers used flugelhorns with trumpet mouthpieces; Terry and Keith Eckert rebuilt one, the same horn Sykes Smith delivered.
101.q: Yeah. Miles. As a matter of fact, Miles had his flugelhorn. He used to call it his fat girl. He’d say, “Hey, man, you ought to take my fat girl home with you. Try it, man. It’s mean.” Miles, Emmett Berry, and Shorty Rogers were three of the cats who had come upon flugelhorns. They were using…

328.t: The trombone he plays now: Worischek and travel case
328.s: The old school trombone he lent J. J., his current large-bore Worischek and flying with it.
328.ch: Practice, Indianapolis memories and the trombone
328.q: It was an old instrument that you use in the schools. I don’t even remember what the name of it was. It wasn’t a very good instrument. That’s for sure.

104.t: Jimmy played cornet, not trumpet or flugelhorn
104.s: Jimmy preferred the cornet's tone; she bought him a flugelhorn but he played it only a few times.
104.q: He did play trumpet, but he didn’t like it. He liked . . . he started very early . . . he really kept to the cornet, because he liked the tone better. Although I did buy him a flugelhorn. He kept saying he’d like to try the flugelhorn, but by the time I bought it for him, I think he wasn’t that…

80.t: Choosing an Olds Recording trumpet in return for his endorsement
80.s: At the factory he was handed papers and picked an Olds Recording trumpet over a Mendez model; Wilson reads the endorsement letter for U.S. Customs.
80.q: So when we get out, and I go around with Vic, and Vic try out, oh half a dozens of horns were in this there, and beautiful factory, and all over these beautiful horns, all that stuff. And Vic would play this one. How would you like to have this ? So, finally, we decided on -- I said I like the…

614.s: Today every trumpeter plays flugelhorn. Dusko Goykovich was an early such player and wrote I Remember Clifford and Woody's Whistle.
614.ch: Instruments, tenors and the current band
614.q: Well, I think the difference in the approach and the whole attitude of my big band today is that everybody plays fluegelhorn. Every trumpet player --

87.s: Willard mentions Quentin Jackson's slide; Young has two horns with different slides and tries new horns on small jobs first.
87.q: Yeah, there are -- there are -- in fact, they build some cases to carry two slides, but I try to get two slides built the same way as possible if I had to, but I don't have two slides. I got two horns, and there's different slide on each horn. But I usually have my favorite horn. Now, just -- just…

27.t: Buescher horns in the band; how Phillips got his Martin trumpet
27.s: Young gave Phillips a Buescher trumpet for Christmas, which he swapped in Jamestown, North Dakota for a gold Martin; the saxes were Bueschers and the C-melodys Conns.
27.q: Yeah. That's where Peggy Lee is from. In Jamestown. So he told me, he says, "I got this horn and I can't play it." He had a gold... Not no gold like they do now. They made gold horns in them days. Burnished gold. And he said it was a Martin. He says, "If you pick up the paint(?) that's on it, you…

382.s: After work on her teeth she took to the flugelhorn, citing Miles Davis and Clark Terry, and carried it around hoping to play.
382.q: Well I practiced for awhile, then I had to have some work done on my teeth. And that's what kept me away from the horn. And by the time my mouth got well enough for me to play, and I looked at myself in the mirror with this horn -- and you couldn't see me for the horn -- I thought I'd try to find…
